_note: Recorded from the frozen Python server (FastMCP 3.4.3) with a real access token, on 2026-11-10. The 'unauthorized' entry is the RAW HTTP exchange: the status, the response headers (including www-authenticate) and the body, exactly as the server sent them. Every other entry is a PARSED, CLIENT-SIDE object, not the raw wire exchange: the values were read off the MCP client's pydantic models and dumped, so they carry pydantic's spellings and defaults (the wire's _meta appears here as 'meta', and members the wire omits appear here as null). The 'tools_list' entry is the client's parsed tool list, with the schemas the client inferred. Compare the shapes, not the byte-for-byte wire text.

tools_list.name: ping
tools_list.description: Health check — returns 'pong'.

tools_list.name: delete_invoice
tools_list.description:
Permanently delete a DRAFT invoice. GATED: first call (no
confirm_token) previews the delete and returns a confirm_token; call
again passing that confirm_token to actually delete. Only DRAFT
invoices can be deleted — invoicing.delete_invoice refuses anything
else.

tools_list.name: delete_bill
tools_list.description:
Permanently delete a DRAFT bill. GATED: first call (no
confirm_token) previews the delete and returns a confirm_token; call
again passing that confirm_token to actually delete. Only DRAFT bills
can be deleted — a bill that has moved past DRAFT already affects AP
and should be voided instead (see void_bill).

tools_list.name: delete_customer
tools_list.description:
Deactivate a customer (soft delete — sets active=False). GATED:
first call (no confirm_token) previews the action and returns a
confirm_token; call again passing that confirm_token to actually
deactivate. Matches the existing DELETE /customers/{id} endpoint:
customers are never hard-deleted anywhere in this app.

tools_list.name: send_invoice_email
tools_list.description:
Email an invoice PDF to a customer. GATED: first call (no
confirm_token) previews the send and returns a confirm_token; call again
passing that confirm_token to actually send. If invoice status is DRAFT
it is promoted to SENT once the email is sent.

tools_list.name: send_payment_reminder
tools_list.description:
Email a payment reminder for an outstanding invoice. GATED: first
call (no confirm_token) previews the send and returns a confirm_token;
call again passing that confirm_token to actually send. Bound to the
invoice's cash still expected (balance_due less unbooked PPh) so a partial
payment between preview and confirm invalidates a stale token. No PDF
is attached — a plain-text/HTML reminder only.

tools_list.description: List vendors, optionally filtered by a name substring.

tools_list.name: resolve_vendor
tools_list.description:
Resolve a vendor name substring to a single vendor id.

Ambiguity-stop primitive: on exactly one match, returns
{"vendor_id": "<uuid>"}. On zero or more than one match, returns
{"candidates": [{"vendor_id", "name"}, ...]} and takes NO other
action — later write tools depend on this exact shape to decide
whether they may proceed automatically or must ask for disambiguation.

profile. Returns {} if not found.

tools_list.name: resolve_customer
tools_list.description:
Resolve a customer name substring to a single customer id.

Ambiguity-stop primitive: on exactly one match, returns
{"customer_id": "<uuid>"}. On zero or more than one match, returns
{"candidates": [{"customer_id", "name"}, ...]} and takes NO other
action — later write tools depend on this exact shape to decide
whether they may proceed automatically or must ask for disambiguation.

tools_list.name: get_business_profile
tools_list.description:
Return the agency's business profile (name, contact, address, etc.).

An uploaded logo is stored as a base64 data URI (often hundreds of KB), so
`logo_url` is replaced by a short placeholder in that case; a regular URL
is returned as-is. `has_logo` says whether any logo is set.

per currency), mirroring GET /api/v1/stats/dashboard (minus

figure).

Delegates all query logic to
`app.services.stats.compute_dashboard_stats`, the same function the
router calls — no duplicated SQL here.

tools_list.name: create_bill
tools_list.description: Create a DRAFT bill. Autonomous.

tools_list.name: update_bill
tools_list.description:
Edit a DRAFT/OPEN bill. `changes` keys are BillUpdate field names (e.g.
notes, payment_terms, discount_type/discount_value, line_items).
Autonomous.

Unknown keys are rejected rather than applied, so a near-miss like "note"
or "terms" errors instead of being dropped by Pydantic's default
extra="ignore" while the tool still reports success.

tools_list.name: create_item
tools_list.description:
Create a catalog item (non-hosting: item_type SERVICE/USAGE/FIXED_FEE).
Autonomous.

Every writable non-hosting ItemCreate field is an explicit arg, including
the revenue/expense account overrides — without them a caller had no way
to post an item to a specific chart-of-accounts line. Hosting fields
(is_hosting, hosting_*, cloudflare_target) are deliberately absent; see
the module docstring.

tools_list.name: update_item
tools_list.description:
Edit an item. `changes` keys are ItemUpdate field names — the same names
`create_item` takes (e.g. name, default_unit_price, active). Autonomous.

Unknown keys are rejected rather than applied: `unit_price` is a near-miss
for `default_unit_price` that Pydantic's default extra="ignore" would
otherwise drop while still returning success.

tools_list.name: create_vendor
tools_list.description:
Create a vendor. Autonomous.

These args are every writable Vendor column. Unlike Customer, Vendor has
no address or phone column at all (see backend/app/models/vendor.py) —
there is nothing further to expose here, and a caller asking to record a
vendor address should be told the field doesn't exist rather than have it
folded into `notes`.

tools_list.name: update_vendor
tools_list.description:
Edit a vendor. `changes` keys are VendorUpdate field names — the same
names `create_vendor` takes (e.g. name, contact_email,
payment_terms_days, tax_id, notes, active). Autonomous.

Unknown keys are rejected rather than applied. This matters most for the
columns Vendor doesn't have: a `changes={"address": ...}` used to return
success while storing nothing.

tools_list.name: create_customer
tools_list.description:
Create a customer. Autonomous.

Every writable customer column is an explicit arg on purpose. When this
tool only exposed name/email/contact-name/currency/notes, a caller asked
for a customer "with phone X at address Y" had nowhere to put either and
ended up folding both into `notes` — the data was in the record but not
in the fields the UI, invoices, and matching read from.

`default_wht_type` (NONE|PPH21|PPH23), `default_wht_rate` (percent) and
`default_wht_gross_up` seed new invoices for this customer; gross-up raises
the invoice so that after the client withholds PPh you still receive the
full base amount.

Address is structured (address1/address2/city/state/postal_code/country),
matching the customer form. The legacy unstructured `billing_address`
column is deliberately not writable here — it is read-only back-compat.

The primary contact name is stored as first/last — the same fields the
customer edit form writes. There is deliberately no combined
`contact_name` arg: the legacy column was dropped in
0024_customer_contact_single because writing it here left records whose
contact name could not be edited in the UI.

tools_list.name: update_customer
tools_list.description:
Edit a customer. `changes` keys are CustomerUpdate field names — the
same names `create_customer` takes (e.g. contact_phone, billing_address1,
billing_city, notes, default_currency, active,
default_wht_type/default_wht_rate/default_wht_gross_up). Gross-up raises the
invoice so that after the client withholds PPh you still receive the full
base amount. Autonomous.

Unknown keys are rejected rather than applied: CustomerUpdate's default
extra="ignore" would otherwise drop a near-miss key like "phone" or
"address" and still return success, the edit silently doing nothing. See
app/mcp/validate.py — every `update_*` tool shares that check.

tools_list.name: create_invoice
tools_list.description:
Create a DRAFT invoice (lands in Awaiting Finalization). Autonomous.

Optional withholding: `wht_type` NONE|PPH21|PPH23, `wht_rate` percent
(defaults 2.5 for PPH21, 2 for PPH23), `wht_gross_up`; gross-up raises the
invoice so that after the client withholds PPh you still receive the full
base amount. Omitted values fall back to the customer's defaults.

tools_list.name: update_invoice
tools_list.description:
Edit a DRAFT invoice. `changes` keys are InvoiceUpdate field names (e.g.
notes, payment_terms, discount_type/discount_value, line_items,
wht_type/wht_rate/wht_gross_up). Gross-up raises the invoice so that after
the client withholds PPh you still receive the full base amount. Autonomous.

Unknown keys are rejected rather than applied, so a near-miss like "note"
or "terms" errors instead of being dropped by Pydantic's default
extra="ignore" while the tool still reports success.

tools_list.name: finalize_invoice
tools_list.description:
Issue a DRAFT invoice (-> OPEN; becomes SENT only when emailed).

Autonomous (internal, reversible via void). A zero-value invoice settles
straight to PAID.

tools_list.name: void_invoice
tools_list.description: Void an invoice (reversible state, not a delete). Autonomous.

tools_list.name: create_recurring_template
tools_list.description:
Create a recurring invoice template (is_template=True, DRAFT).
`schedule` matches RecurringSchedule fields (frequency, interval,
start_date, end_mode, end_date?, end_after_cycles?). Optional withholding
via `wht_type` NONE|PPH21|PPH23, `wht_rate`, `wht_gross_up`; gross-up
raises the invoice so that after the client withholds PPh you still
receive the full base amount. Autonomous.

tools_list.name: trigger_recurring
tools_list.description:
Manually trigger one recurring cycle for a template — idempotent per
(template_id, cycle_key). Autonomous.

tools_list.name: create_project
tools_list.description: Create a project. Autonomous.

tools_list.name: update_project
tools_list.description:
Edit a project. `changes` keys are ProjectUpdate field names — the same
names `create_project` takes (e.g. code, name, currency, status,
contract_value, notes, active). Autonomous.

Unknown keys are rejected rather than applied, so a near-miss like
"project_name" errors instead of being dropped by Pydantic's default
extra="ignore" while the tool still reports success.

tools_list.name: create_quotation
tools_list.description: Create a DRAFT quotation. Autonomous.

tools_list.name: update_quotation
tools_list.description:
Edit a DRAFT/SENT quotation. `changes` keys are QuotationUpdate field
names (e.g. notes, payment_terms, discount_type/discount_value,
line_items). Autonomous.

Unknown keys are rejected rather than applied, so a near-miss like "note"
or "valid_till" (real field: `valid_until`) errors instead of being dropped
by Pydantic's default extra="ignore" while the tool still reports success.

tools_list.name: resolve_reconciliation_match
tools_list.description:
Force-resolve a PENDING_MANUAL_REVIEW payment against a chosen
invoice. Safe-stop: refuses — returns {"error": ...}, no side effect,
payment status unchanged — on any currency or amount mismatch between
the payment and the invoice; a human must resolve those via the
ManualReviewView UI. Autonomous only for an exact currency+amount
match (the payer/date ambiguity that put it in the queue).
